sentences.nl: Het is de laatste avond van de Dutch Summer School.
sentences.en: It is the last evening of the Dutch Summer School.

sentences.nl: Alle studenten zijn naar de barbecue gekomen.
sentences.en: All the students came to the barbecue.

sentences.nl: Tijdens deze barbecue krijgen ze hun certificaat.
sentences.en: During this barbecue, they will receive their certificate.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• During this barbecue get they their certificate.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Tijdens" is a preposition meaning "during," used to indicate when something happens.  
• "Deze" is a demonstrative pronoun meaning "this," used for singular de-nouns.  
• "Krijgen" is the verb "to get" or "to receive," in the present tense. The subject "ze" (they) comes after the verb due to the inverted word order in main clauses starting with elements other than the subject.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Tijdens de zomer gaan we naar het strand." (During the summer, we go to the beach.)  
  - "Ze krijgen hun diploma in juni." (They receive their diploma in June.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Tijdens de vergadering bespreken we het project. (During the meeting, we discuss the project.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it is common to have casual barbecues during summer months where both socializing and informal ceremonies, like handing out certificates, can take place.

sentences.nl: Bart houdt een toespraak.
sentences.en: Bart is giving a speech.

sentences.nl: Beste studenten,, ik heb van de docent gehoord, dat jullie heel hard hebben gestudeerd.
sentences.en: Dear students, I have heard from the teacher that you have studied very hard.

sentences.nl: Ik hoop dat jullie Nederlands veel is verbeterd.
sentences.en: I hope that your Dutch has improved a lot.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Ik hoop dat jullie Nederlands veel is verbeterd.  
  "I hope that your Dutch much is improved."

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik hoop dat" (I hope that): A common structure to express hope or expectation.  
• "jullie Nederlands" (your Dutch): "jullie" is the plural form for "your," and "Nederlands" is the noun referring to the Dutch language.  
• "veel is verbeterd" (much is improved): "veel" means "much" and modifies "verbeterd" (improved), which is in the past participle form and used here in a passive construction.  

Extra Examples:  
• "Ik hoop dat hij op tijd komt." (I hope that he comes on time.)  
• "Jullie Duits is erg goed geworden." (Your German has become very good.)  
• "Hij heeft veel geleerd." (He has learned a lot.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik denk dat jullie Frans ook vooruit is gegaan." (I think that your French has also progressed.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, learning multiple languages is common, especially English, German, and French, due to the country's geographical location and international trade.

sentences.nl: Ook ben ik blij dat jullie op veel plekken in Drenthe zijn geweest.
sentences.en: I am also glad that you have been to many places in Drenthe.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Also am I happy that you in many places in Drenthe have been.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ook" is an adverb meaning "also" and can start a sentence for emphasis.  
• "Ben ik blij" uses inversion, a common structure where the verb precedes the subject in main clauses for emphasis or after adverbs.  
• "Dat jullie op veel plekken in Drenthe zijn geweest" is a subordinate clause introduced by "dat," which changes the word order, placing the verb at the end.

Extra examples:  
• "Ook ga ik morgen naar de markt." (Also, I am going to the market tomorrow.)  
• "Ik ben blij dat je het leuk vond." (I am happy that you liked it.)  
• "Ze zijn op veel plekken in Nederland geweest." (They have been to many places in the Netherlands.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ook vind ik het leuk dat jullie samen hebben gewerkt." (I also like that you have worked together.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Drenthe is a province in the Netherlands known for its natural beauty, including national parks and prehistoric dolmens. It is a popular destination for those interested in outdoor activities and history.

sentences.nl: Jullie kennen het Nederlandse platteland nu een beetje beter.
sentences.en: You now know the Dutch countryside a bit better.

sentences.nl: Ik hoop natuurlijk ook dat jullie nog niet alles hebben geleerd.
sentences.en: Of course, I also hope that you haven't learned everything yet.

sentences.nl: En ik zeg dat,, omdat ik jullie graag de volgende keer opnieuw hier zie,, op onze Winter School, of volgend jaar op de Summer School.
sentences.en: And I say that because I would like to see you here again next time at our Winter School or next year at the Summer School.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And I say that, because I you all gladly the next time again here see, at our Winter School, or next year at the Summer School.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En ik zeg dat" (And I say that): Coordinating conjunction "en" starts the sentence. "Dat" introduces a subordinate clause.  
• "omdat ik jullie graag de volgende keer opnieuw hier zie" (because I you all gladly the next time again here see): "omdat" introduces a reason; verb "zie" (see) goes to the end of the clause.  
• "op onze Winter School, of volgend jaar op de Summer School" (at our Winter School, or next year at the Summer School): Prepositions "op" and "of" are used to indicate location and alternatives.

Examples:  
• "Ik hoop dat jullie het leuk vinden." (I hope that you all like it.)  
• "Omdat ik morgen vrij ben, ga ik naar het strand." (Because I am free tomorrow, I am going to the beach.)  
• "Volgend jaar gaan we naar Frankrijk op vakantie." (Next year we are going to France on vacation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Omdat ik jullie graag zie, nodig ik jullie uit voor het diner." (Because I like to see you all, I invite you for dinner.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The concept of "Winter School" and "Summer School" is less common in the Netherlands than in some other countries, but such programs can be found at international schools or universities offering specialized courses during breaks.

sentences.nl: Voordat ik de certificaten uitreik,, wil ik vragen of Marieke even naar voren komt.
sentences.en: Before I hand out the certificates, I would like to ask Marieke to come forward.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Before I the certificates hand out, I want to ask if Marieke just to front comes.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Voordat" is a subordinating conjunction that introduces a subordinate clause, causing the verb "uitreik" to be placed at the end of the clause.  
• "Wil ik vragen" uses inversion, a common structure in Dutch where the subject and verb are inverted after an introductory element like a subordinate clause.  
• "Even" is a common Dutch particle used to soften requests, similar to "just" or "a moment" in English.

Examples:  
• Voordat we vertrekken, moeten we alles controleren. (Before we leave, we need to check everything.)  
• Kun je even wachten? (Can you wait a moment?)  
• Wil je even helpen met de boodschappen? (Do you want to help with the groceries for a moment?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Voordat de vergadering begint, wil ik iedereen welkom heten. (Before the meeting starts, I want to welcome everyone.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it’s common to use “even” to make requests sound more polite and less direct. It reflects the Dutch preference for politeness and indirectness in communication.

sentences.nl: Vinden jullie dat Marieke goed les heeft gegeven? — ‘Ja!’ roepen de studenten.
sentences.en: Do you think Marieke taught well? — 'Yes!' the students shout.

sentences.nl: Geef haar dan een warm applaus!
sentences.en: Then give her a warm round of applause!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Give her then a warm applause!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "Geef" is in the imperative form, used for giving commands.  
• "Dan" here means "then" and is used to suggest timing or sequence.  
• "Een warm applaus" is a direct object phrase, meaning "a warm applause."  
• Example sentence: "Geef hem een kans." (Give him a chance.)  
• Example sentence: "Dan gaan we eten." (Then we will eat.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Geef ons nu een moment van stilte. (Give us a moment of silence now.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, giving someone a warm applause is a common way to show appreciation and encouragement during events or performances.

sentences.nl: De studenten klappen voor Marieke.
sentences.en: The students applaud for Marieke.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The students clap for Marieke.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De studenten" is the subject, meaning "The students," showing a definite plural noun.  
• "Klappen" is the verb meaning "clap" in the present tense, used here in a simple action sentence.  
• "Voor" is a preposition meaning "for," indicating the recipient of the action.  
• "Marieke" is a proper noun, the object of the preposition, so no article is needed.

• Extra examples:  
  - "De kinderen zingen voor de leraar." (The children sing for the teacher.)  
  - "Wij wachten op de bus." (We are waiting for the bus.)  
  - "Zij zorgen voor de planten." (They take care of the plants.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De muzikanten spelen voor het publiek. (The musicians play for the audience.)  

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, clapping to show appreciation during events or performances is common, similar to many Western cultures.

sentences.nl: En dan is het nu tijd voor de certificaten!
sentences.en: And now it's time for the certificates!

sentences.nl: Bart reikt de certificaten uit.
sentences.en: Bart hands out the certificates.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Bart hands the certificates out.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Reikt uit" is a separable verb, meaning "to hand out" or "to distribute." The particle "uit" separates from the verb in the sentence.  
• The sentence follows a simple subject-verb-object structure.  
• Example 1: Zij reikt de prijzen uit. (She hands the prizes out.)  
• Example 2: De leraar reikt de rapporten uit. (The teacher distributes the reports.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Jan reikt de uitnodigingen uit. (Jan hands out the invitations.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch schools and workplaces, it's common to have ceremonies or meetings where certificates or awards are handed out to recognize achievements, often accompanied by a small celebration.

sentences.nl: Ik heb hem gisteren overhoord.
sentences.en: I quizzed him yesterday.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Ik heb hem gisteren overhoord.  
  (I have him yesterday quizzed/tested.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present perfect tense ("heb overhoord"), which is common for past actions that have relevance to the present.  
• "Hem" is the object pronoun meaning "him." Dutch pronouns often follow the auxiliary verb in perfect tense structures.  
• "Overhoren" is a separable verb. In the perfect tense, "over" and "hoord" are split, with "over" moving to the end of the sentence.  
• Example: "Hij heeft haar gisteren gebeld." (He called her yesterday.)  
• Example: "Wij hebben het boek al gelezen." (We have already read the book.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ik heb haar vorige week geholpen. (I helped her last week.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Overhoren" typically refers to a teacher or parent quizzing a student or child about their homework or study material, reflecting the importance of education and parental involvement in Dutch culture.

sentences.nl: Hij kent nog niet eens 20 bladzijdes!
sentences.en: He doesn't even know 20 pages yet!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He knows yet not even 20 pages!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij kent" means "he knows." The verb "kennen" is used for familiarity with something.  
• "Nog niet eens" is a phrase meaning "not even yet," used to emphasize the lack of progress or extent.  
• Word order: "kent nog niet eens" is in a typical Dutch sentence structure with the verb second and the negation phrase following.  
• Example: "Ze heeft nog niet eens gegeten." (She hasn't even eaten yet.)  
• Example: "Ik heb nog niet eens tijd gehad." (I haven't even had time yet.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij heeft nog niet eens de film gezien." (She hasn't even seen the movie yet.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, being familiar with something often implies a deeper understanding or engagement. The phrase "nog niet eens" can emphasize surprise or disappointment at what someone hasn't done or achieved.

sentences.nl: Gianluca is een leuke jongen.
sentences.en: Gianluca is a nice boy.

sentences.nl: Hij kan hele mooie complimenten maken.
sentences.en: He can give very nice compliments.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He can whole beautiful compliments make.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij kan" uses the modal verb "kan" (can), which is placed before the main verb in Dutch sentences.  
• The adjective "hele" (whole) is used here for emphasis, similar to "really" or "very" in English.  
• "Maken" (to make) is the main verb, placed at the end of the clause, which is typical in Dutch subordinate clauses and sentences with modal verbs.  
• Extra examples:  
  - "Zij kan goed zingen." (She can sing well.)  
  - "Hij maakt vaak grapjes." (He often makes jokes.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij kan hele lekkere taarten bakken. (She can bake really delicious cakes.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Compliments in Dutch culture are often sincere and specific, focusing on personal achievements or characteristics rather than general or exaggerated praise.

sentences.nl: Maar hij is mijn type niet.
sentences.en: But he is not my type.

sentences.nl: Geef mij maar een lieve, en een beetje onhandige jongen.
sentences.en: Just give me a sweet and slightly awkward boy.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Give me just a sweet, and a bit clumsy boy.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Geef mij maar" is an informal way to say "just give me" or "I'll take." "Maar" here softens the request, making it less direct or demanding.  
• "Een lieve, en een beetje onhandige jongen" uses adjectives "lieve" (sweet) and "onhandige" (clumsy) to describe "jongen" (boy). Note the use of the article "een" before each adjective-noun pair, which is common in Dutch to emphasize different qualities.  
• Example Sentences:  
  - "Geef mij maar een kopje koffie." (Just give me a cup of coffee.)  
  - "Ze wil een grote, en een beetje oude auto." (She wants a big, and somewhat old car.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Geef mij maar een warme, en een beetje zoute soep." (Just give me a warm, and a bit salty soup.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
- In Dutch culture, the phrase "Geef mij maar" is often used in informal contexts when expressing a preference, especially in settings like cafes or casual dining, where politeness is appreciated but directness is also common.

sentences.en: Like Martin, for example…

sentences.nl: Dat is nou echt een leuke jongen!
sentences.en: That is really a nice guy!

sentences.nl: Ik ga hem even zoeken,, want hij wilde mij vanavond de maan laten zien!
sentences.en: I'm going to look for him, because he wanted to show me the moon tonight!

sentences.nl: Maar… ondertussen…, is Martin al bij het bruggetje…, en je raadt al met wie…
sentences.en: But… in the meantime…, Martin is already at the little bridge…, and you can guess with whom…

sentences.nl: Dit was ‘Heb je zin?’
sentences.en: This was 'Are you in the mood?'

sentences.nl: En voorlopig was dat de laatste aflevering.
sentences.en: And for now, that was the last episode.

sentences.nl: Misschien is het goed om te weten, dat je zelf natuurlijk ook naar de Summer School kunt komen.
sentences.en: Perhaps it's good to know that you can of course also come to the Summer School yourself.

sentences.nl: Wil je veel Nederlands leren in een korte tijd? — Wil je mensen leren kennen uit de hele wereld? — Tijdens een gezellige vakantie in Nederland? — Kom dan naar de Dutch Summer School, of de Dutch Winter School!
sentences.en: Do you want to learn a lot of Dutch in a short time? — Do you want to meet people from all over the world? — During a pleasant vacation in the Netherlands? — Then come to the Dutch Summer School, or the Dutch Winter School!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Want you much Dutch learn in a short time? — Want you people get to know from the whole world? — During a pleasant holiday in Netherlands? — Come then to the Dutch Summer School, or the Dutch Winter School!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Questions with "Wil je":** The sentence begins with "Wil je" (Do you want), which is a common way to form yes/no questions in Dutch by starting with the verb.  
• **Prepositions "in" and "uit":** "In een korte tijd" (in a short time) uses "in" for time duration, while "uit de hele wereld" (from the whole world) uses "uit" to denote origin.  
• **Conjunction "of":** Used here to mean "or," linking two options (Dutch Summer School, Dutch Winter School).

Examples:  
- Wil je koffie drinken? (Do you want to drink coffee?)  
- Ken je mensen uit andere landen? (Do you know people from other countries?)  
- Kom dan naar ons feest! (Then come to our party!)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Wil je snel Nederlands spreken in een leuke omgeving? (Do you want to speak Dutch quickly in a fun environment?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Dutch Summer School and Winter School are popular programs for intensive Dutch language learning, drawing international students who want to immerse themselves in Dutch culture and language.

sentences.nl: Meer informatie vind je op, dutchsummerschool.nl, en dutchwinterschool.nl
sentences.en: You can find more information at dutchsummerschool.nl and dutchwinterschool.nl.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• More information find you on, dutchsummerschool.nl, and dutchwinterschool.nl.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence demonstrates a basic Dutch sentence structure where the verb "vind" (find) comes before the subject "je" (you) because it is an imperative sentence.  
• The use of "op" (on) as a preposition here is standard for websites or locations.  
• "Meer informatie" (more information) is a common phrase used in both written and spoken Dutch. 

Examples:  
• "Meer informatie over de cursus vind je op onze website." (More information about the course you find on our website.)  
• "Op maandag beginnen de lessen." (On Monday the lessons start.)  
• "Je vindt de details op de laatste pagina." (You find the details on the last page.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Meer details vind je in de handleiding." (You find more details in the manual.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Netherlands is known for its high proficiency in English, and many educational programs, such as the Dutch Summer and Winter Schools, cater to international audiences looking to learn Dutch.

sentences.nl: En wie weet, sta jij straks zelf op dat bruggetje, met iemand naar de maan te kijken, terwijl je Nederlands praat.
sentences.en: And who knows, maybe soon you'll be standing on that little bridge yourself, watching the moon with someone, while speaking Dutch.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And who knows, stand you soon yourself on that little bridge, with someone to the moon to watch, while you Dutch speak.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En wie weet" (And who knows) is a common phrase used to introduce possibilities or uncertainties.  
• "Sta jij straks zelf" (stand you soon yourself) uses "sta" (stand), emphasizing a future position or scenario. "Straks" implies a near future.  
• "Met iemand naar de maan te kijken" (with someone to the moon to watch) uses "te + infinitive" for ongoing or continuous actions.  
• "Terwijl je Nederlands praat" (while you Dutch speak) uses "terwijl" to indicate simultaneous actions.

Examples:  
- "En wie weet, vind je morgen de oplossing." (And who knows, you might find the solution tomorrow.)  
- "Straks ga je zelf koken." (Soon you will cook yourself.)  
- "Met iemand te praten is soms moeilijk." (Talking with someone is sometimes difficult.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En wie weet, reis jij straks naar een ander land, terwijl je nieuwe vrienden maakt. (And who knows, you might soon travel to another country, while making new friends.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The mention of "naar de maan kijken" (looking at the moon) can be seen as a romantic or idyllic activity, often associated with peaceful or introspective moments in Dutch culture.

sentences.nl: Hoewel het erg veel werk was,, heb ik deze lessen met heel veel plezier gemaakt.
sentences.en: Although it was a lot of work, I created these lessons with great pleasure.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Although it very much work was, have I these lessons with very much pleasure made.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoewel" is a subordinating conjunction that introduces a subordinate clause, affecting the word order by moving the verb to the end of the clause.  
• "Erg veel" means "very much" or "a lot," and is used to emphasize quantity or degree.  
• The past perfect tense ("heb gemaakt") is used to describe an action that was completed in the past.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hoewel het regende, gingen we toch naar buiten." (Although it rained, we still went outside.)  
  - "Ik heb het boek met veel interesse gelezen." (I read the book with much interest.)  
  - "Hoewel hij moe was, bleef hij tot laat werken." (Although he was tired, he stayed up late working.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hoewel het koud was, gingen we zwemmen. (Although it was cold, we went swimming.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, expressing enjoyment in doing work or tasks, even if they are challenging, is common and reflects a positive work ethic.

sentences.nl: Ik weet niet of ik meer van deze filmpjes moet maken,, of dat ik mijn tijd moet gebruiken, voor andere lesmaterialen.
sentences.en: I don't know if I should make more of these videos, or if I should use my time for other teaching materials.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I know not if I more of these videos must make, or that I my time must use, for other teaching materials.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses a subordinate clause structure with "of" (if, whether) and "dat" (that) to introduce alternative options.  
• The verb "moet" (must) appears in both clauses, indicating necessity or obligation.  
• Word order in Dutch subordinate clauses typically puts the verb at the end.

Examples:  
• Ik weet niet of hij komt, of dat hij thuis blijft. (I don't know if he is coming, or that he will stay home.)  
• Zij vraagt zich af of ze moet gaan, of dat ze kan blijven. (She wonders if she should go, or that she can stay.)  
• We moeten beslissen of we hier eten, of dat we naar een restaurant gaan. (We need to decide if we eat here, or that we go to a restaurant.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ik vraag me af of ik deze baan moet accepteren, of dat ik verder moet zoeken. (I wonder if I should accept this job, or that I should keep looking.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, directness is valued, and asking questions about priorities or decisions, such as whether to focus on one task over another, reflects a pragmatic approach to time management.

sentences.nl: Wat vinden jullie? — Vinden jullie deze filmpjes leuk? — Wil je dat ik met een nieuwe reeks kom? — Wil je weten of Martin en Marieke, misschien toch bij elkaar komen? — Laat het mij weten!
sentences.en: What do you think? — Do you like these videos? — Do you want me to come up with a new series? — Do you want to know if Martin and Marieke might end up together after all? — Let me know!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• What think you (plural)? — Think you (plural) these videos fun? — Want you that I with a new series come? — Want you to know if Martin and Marieke, perhaps still together come? — Let it me know!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• In Dutch, "vinden" is used similarly to "think" or "find" in English, especially in the context of opinions.  
• "Jullie" is the plural form of "you."  
• "Laat het mij weten" uses imperative form; "laat" is the command form of "laten" (to let).  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Wat denk je?" (What do you think?)  
  - "Vind je deze film leuk?" (Do you like this movie?)  
  - "Laat me weten wanneer je aankomt." (Let me know when you arrive.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wat vinden jullie van het nieuwe restaurant?" (What do you think of the new restaurant?)

## 4. Culture Note  
• In Dutch culture, directness is often appreciated. Asking for opinions directly, as seen in the sentence, is common and expected in many social interactions.

sentences.nl: Schrijf je commentaar onder de video!
sentences.en: Write your comment under the video!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Write your comment under the video!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Schrijf" is the imperative form of "schrijven" (to write). In imperative sentences, the verb typically comes first.  
• "Je" is a possessive pronoun meaning "your."  
• "Onder" is a preposition meaning "under." Prepositions in Dutch often relate to physical position or metaphorical context.

sentences.en: And you can always help me in the following way: by clicking on the thumbs-up, and by sharing the video on social media... because the more people watch these videos, the greater the chance that I will come up with a new series!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And you can me always in the following way help: by on the thumbs-up to click, and by the video on social media to share..., because how more people these videos watch, how greater the chance that I with a new series come!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word order in Dutch can be flexible but follows the Subject-Verb-Object structure, especially noticeable in subordinate clauses like "hoe meer mensen deze video's bekijken."  
• The phrase "op de volgende manier" (in the following way) is a common way to introduce instructions or steps.  
• "Hoe...hoe..." structure is used to indicate a correlation or a conditional relationship (the more…the more…).  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Je kunt me helpen door op de knop te drukken." (You can help me by pressing the button.)  
  - "Hoe sneller je werkt, hoe eerder je klaar bent." (The faster you work, the sooner you are done.)  
  - "Ze deelde haar verhaal op social media." (She shared her story on social media.)

## 3. Create a New Example
